name: Coreopsis

project_scope.note: All FOUR Coreopsis taxa exist in the canonical manifest. C. lanceolata is a legitimately installed learner card but native-target-zone status is UNRESOLVED and excluded from confirmed-native metrics. C. wrightii is a distinct accepted Kew/USDA-GRIN concept while FNA folds it within C. basalis. Preserve scientific ambiguity, no taxonomy/range changed.

study_strategy.warning: Many Asteraceae look similar from a distance. Use head structure and involucre details, not just a yellow flower photo.

curation_status.rights_note: Six source photos noncommercial or rights-review; no all-rights-reserved basalis image reused; the single lanceolata photo is CC BY. Existing species source status/range labels preserved.

b067_study_strategy.warning: Coreopsis wrightii has been synonymized with C. basalis in older ITIS/FNA treatments, but current Kew accepts it as a distinct species. Preserve that conflict explicitly.

quick_split: C. basalis — slender annual with finely divided leaves and yellow rays commonly showing a dark basal blotch.
C. tinctoria — branching annual with threadlike divided foliage and strongly bicolored yellow/red-brown rays.

C. wrightii — slender annual with narrow linear leaves; yellow rays usually have rusty-red to maroon basal markings and 3-toothed tips. Older treatments may merge it with C. basalis, so use the full character package.

C. lanceolata — comparison-only HOLD; perennial, with basal/proximal leaves that are simple or only lightly lobed and broadly lanceolate to oblanceolate relative to the finely divided annual project species.
b067_comparison_lesson.hold_rule: Do not use cultivated C. lanceolata or plant-sale records to satisfy the project's target-zone native-range threshold.

recognition.where_to_look_first: For the project set, start with life cycle and leaf architecture before judging ray color. Then compare the distribution and intensity of red-brown basal ray markings, plant branching, and head size.
priority: finely divided/threadlike versus narrow-linear versus broader simple/lobed leaves
where leaves are concentrated on the stem
ray color pattern, especially basal red-brown markings
cypsela characters only when vegetative and floral traits remain ambiguous
recognition.warning: Coreopsis is morphologically broad as a genus, and early versus later leaves can differ on the same plant. Use the complete character set rather than ray color alone.

visual_needs: side-by-side whole plants of C. basalis, C. tinctoria, and C. wrightii at similar scale
leaf architecture comparison: finely divided basalis, threadlike-divided tinctoria, narrow-linear wrightii
ray-base comparison showing the dark/bicolored markings across the three annual anchors
exact displayable C. wrightii habit, leaf, and head closeups
C. lanceolata comparison image only as an explicitly labeled HOLD, emphasizing broader simple/lightly lobed leaves and perennial habit
annotated basalis-versus-wrightii comparison because historical treatments can blur that pair
source_notes: Flora of North America notes broad variation in Coreopsis leaf arrangement and dissection and warns that early leaves can differ strongly from later leaves.
FNA treats C. lanceolata as a perennial with simple or lightly lobed lanceolate-to-oblanceolate leaves, useful as a visual contrast but not a range-approved project species.
fast_fill_note: C. basalis and C. tinctoria retain existing image galleries; C. wrightii now has a 3-view private-study UT Austin BIO406D PlantPics diagnostic set (habit, flower head, leaf/stem arrangement). C. lanceolata remains comparison-only HOLD and is not promoted by visual work.

look_here_first: START by deciding PERENNIAL versus ANNUAL and checking WHERE LEAVES ARE FOUND ON THE STEM. C. lanceolata = perennial with a basal/lower cluster of broad simple or weakly lobed lance-shaped leaves, long mostly leafless flowering stalks, and usually plain yellow rays. C. basalis, C. tinctoria and C. wrightii = usually slender annuals with divided leaves and rays often marked red/brown near their bases. NEXT compare complete mid-stem leaf lobes (their WIDTH and pinnate division), flowering branch lengths, and the SIDE and BACK of a head: outer CALYCULAR BRACELETS (calyculus) versus INNER PHYLLARIES. The KEY C. basalis versus C. wrightii is taxonomically disputed: FNA combines them whereas Kew/USDA treat wrightii separately, so label ambiguous intermediates and DO NOT force IDs from one reddish ray mark.
shared_traits: Tickseeds have composite ASTERACEAE 'FLOWER HEADS' (CAPITULA), not single flowers: showy outer RAY FLORETS surround many central DISK FLORETS; ray petals are actually the straps (ligules) of individual florets.

Beneath the flower head are two diagnostic layers to inspect in this group: an outer CALYCULUS of small green bractlets, and inner INVOLUCRAL PHYLLARIES (the bracts immediately supporting the entire head). Separate outer from inner when counting or comparing.
Leaves may be basal and stem-borne (cauline), often opposite but variable; annual species typically have more divided foliage, while C. lanceolata often keeps broader lower leaves.
Fruit is an individual dry CYPSELA (achene-like one-seeded fruit) per fertile floret; wing and pappus detail is a high-value technical character and normally requires a millimeter macro.
Yellow rays with dark red or brown bases occur in basalis, tinctoria, and wrightii; pattern variation makes flower color UNRELIABLE as a strict species key.

genus_diagnostics.head: Look at ONE flower HEAD from front and from below. The outer petal-like yellow straps belong to separate RAY FLORETS; the darker or yellow central area is MANY small DISK FLORETS. A head is a cluster/inflorescence, not one huge flower.
genus_diagnostics.calyculus: Outside/under the capitulum, find the OUTER ring of narrow CALYCULAR BRACTLETS—the small green leaflike pieces pointing or spreading below the head. A macro at the correct side angle and a millimeter scale is required before using size differences.
genus_diagnostics.phyllary: Inside the calyculus and nearer the disk are the broader INNER PHYLLARIES (true involucre bracts); do not confuse them with individual ray petals, outer calycular bractlets, or sepals of individual flowers.
genus_diagnostics.rays: RAY FLORETS frequently have yellow ligules with a red-brown basal patch in the three annual taxa. In C. tinctoria the maroon portion can occupy much of a ray; in C. basalis/wrightii it often remains a shorter proximal spot/band. Flower color changes and overlaps—supporting evidence only.
genus_diagnostics.disc: Central DISK florets are small separate flowers with their own corolla and reproductive parts. Disc coloration differs in some FNA treatments (C. basalis distal reddish disc lobes; C. lanceolata yellow) but a macro and source taxonomy are needed before a firm ID arrow.
genus_diagnostics.leaves: Compare an entire mature MID-STEM LEAF with SCALE: C. tinctoria leaves commonly 1–3 times pinnate with narrow/threadlike divisions; basalis leaves can be 1–2-pinnately lobed, often somewhat wider; wrightii generally narrower linear lobes in the segregate concept (yet broad overlap); lanceolata basal/lower leaves simple or only lightly lobed and markedly wider.
genus_diagnostics.habit: ANNUAL basalis/tinctoria/wrightii generally have several flowering branch points and leaves up the stem; PERENNIAL lanceolata has a clump of lower leaves and long often leafless peduncles. This is a field cue, not a county-native status.
genus_diagnostics.cypsela: A CYPSELA is the individual seedlike fruit of one composite floret. Compare shape, edge wings, and pappus awns/scales using a ruler: FNA basalis wingless, tinctoria sometimes winged, lanceolata more spreading papery wings. Wrightii taxonomy concept makes historical basalis fruit interpretation important.

quick_key.if: Rhizomatous/clump-forming PERENNIAL; wide mostly basal/lower simple or lightly lobed leaves; long near-leafless flower stalks; rays generally plain yellow
quick_key.then: C. lanceolata — canonical learner; target-zone native range UNRESOLVED, comparison not confirmed native

quick_key.if: Slender ANNUAL; leaves dissected into many very narrow/threadlike divisions; larger or variable maroon/red-brown portion at ray bases
quick_key.then: C. tinctoria — check shorter outer bractlets and disc/ray proportions, not maroon alone

quick_key.if: Slender ANNUAL; leaves simple to deeply divided, generally wider terminal leaf lobes and red-brown basal flecks/spots on yellow rays
quick_key.then: C. basalis under FNA broadly; segregate C. wrightii can look similar

quick_key.if: Slender ANNUAL in Central Texas; particularly narrow linear middle/upper leaf divisions and usually slender stems; reddish ray-base spots
quick_key.then: C. wrightii under Kew/GRIN accepted segregation — compare a voucher, leaf/lobe widths and head characters; FNA merges within C. basalis

quick_key.if: No leaves shown, only a two-colored head; bracts/fruit out of focus
quick_key.then: Coreopsis cf. basalis / wrightii / tinctoria as appropriate; photograph foliage, head underside and cypselae before forcing a species

comparison_cards.title: Goldenmane vs plains tickseed
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Start at the COMPLETE mid-stem leaf: basalis variable lobed leaves often broader; tinctoria frequently further subdivided into almost threadlike ultimate lobes. Inspect the calyculus bractlets (size) and mature cypsela margins. Both may carry yellow rays with a red-brown base, so the paint-like ring is not decisive.
photo_requirements: matched mature whole leaves from similar stem level
same-scale underside of capitula showing outer calyculus vs inner phyllaries
mature cypsela macro with mm scale
comparison_cards.caution: Existing gallery photos are not yet audited macro proof of precise leaf-lobe widths or fruit-edge wings.

comparison_cards.title: Goldenmane versus Wright's tickseed: a taxonomic split
comparison_cards.look_here_first: The wrightii segregate tends to have narrower middle/upper leaf divisions and slender habits, while typical basalis often has broader divisions; however FNA subsumes the narrow western populations into basalis. Use voucher-based concept, complete leaf, head underside and local range; record uncertainty.
photo_requirements: species-vouchered local full mid-stem leaves, matching scale
physical rights-cleared wrightii images; UT PlantPics links are EXTERNAL only
comparison_cards.caution: Never claim the narrow-leaf character is an absolutely accepted species boundary across all authorities.

comparison_cards.title: Annual tickseeds vs lance-leaved perennial
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Look to the plant BASE: lanceolata typically a perennial with broader mostly lower simple/lobed leaves and long often leafless flower stems; the other three are generally annual, much more finely divided foliage. Compare full habit and lower leaves, not a single golden ray.
photo_requirements: whole plants including ground-level leaves and basal crowns
lanceolata actual foliage macro and noncultivated habitat voucher
comparison_cards.caution: C. lanceolata is installed learner-only with range UNRESOLVED; inclusion is not proof of native target-zone status.

comparison_cards.title: Which is ray, disk, calyculus or phyllary?
comparison_cards.look_here_first: The outer yellow 'petal' is a RAY FLORET ligule; the center is dozens of tiny DISK FLORETS. Under the head is the OUTER CALYCULUS of bractlets and the INNER INVOLUCRAL PHYLLARIES. To identify a specimen, take front, side and underside photos and a mature fruit macro.
photo_requirements: same head's underside outer calyculus vs inner phyllaries with arrows after actual coordinates checked
comparison_cards.caution: Present images are head/plant references; do not invent arrow positions for tiny separate parts.

visual_comparison.title: Coreopsis: look below the flowers before naming a tickseed
visual_comparison.subtitle: Seven already installed exact-species learner photos: three C. basalis, three C. tinctoria and one C. lanceolata. C. wrightii is linked as a noninstalled educational reference and NOT counted as local photo coverage. No fabricated anatomical arrows.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: PERENNIAL broad lower leaves = LANCEOLATA (range unresolved). ANNUAL threadlike/feathery leaves = often TINCTORIA. ANNUAL variable broader divided leaf = BASALIS; very narrow western segregate = WRIGHTII (taxonomic disagreement). Count OUTER calycular bractlets vs INNER phyllaries; do not ID by the red eye.
